name: record_intake
description: Save facts the person has given about their symptoms, situation, location and travel radius. Call it every time you learn a new fact; pass only the new fields, and the app merges them into one intake record. Record red flags as soon as you spot them. Returns the merged intake record and missing_required, a list of required fields still missing (location and travel_radius before a facility search; at least one symptom or red flag before get_care_level).

name: get_care_level
description: Get the suggested level of care from TriAgent's triage rules (triage/triage_rules.yaml), based on the current intake record. Red flags are checked first, then the symptom rule, then modifiers; when unsure the higher level wins. Call it after the main symptoms and any red flags are recorded, and again if the person adds a symptom or says it's getting worse. Use the returned level as given and never lower it. Returns: level (call_911, er, urgent_care, clinic_or_telehealth, or self_care), label, reason (one plain-language sentence), rule_id (the red flag or symptom rule that fired), watch_for (signs that would mean a higher level), modifiers, and missing (unanswered intake fields that could raise the level; ask about these before searching).

name: find_care_nearby
description: Find facilities for a level of care near the person, using Google Maps Platform (Places for facilities, Distance Matrix for travel time). Location, travel radius and transport come from the intake record, which must have location and travel_radius. Never call it for call_911. Returns up to 8 results, each with name, care_type, address, distance, travel_time, open_now, phone, in_radius (false means outside the person's radius), low_cost (community health center or free clinic) and maps_url. Returns an empty list if nothing is found.

level.description: The level exactly as get_care_level returned it.

open_now_only.description: True to return only places open now. Use for er and urgent_care, or when the person needs care today.

include_low_cost.description: True to also search community health centers and free clinics. Use when the person has no insurance or mentions cost.

name: offer_choices
description: Show tappable answer chips under your question on the web page, so the person can answer with one tap instead of typing. Call it whenever your question has a short set of likely answers: travel radius, how long symptoms have lasted, age band, yes or no, transport, insurance, or a short checklist of symptoms. Put the question in the question field (and in your reply text too, if you like); the page always shows the question above the chips. Call this tool once per turn. The person can always type something else instead. Never call it in an emergency reply. Returns {"shown": true}; add no more text after calling it.

question.description: The one question you are asking, as a short sentence (for example "How far are you willing to travel?").

options.description: 2 to 6 short answers, written the way the person would say them (for example "5 miles", "10 miles", "25 miles", "50 miles").

multiple.description: True when the person may pick more than one, such as a checklist of symptoms. Include a "None of these" option in that case.
